name: collections-c-dbedaf95-blind21
instr:
# Collections-C: diagnosing 21 injected faults without a test suite

The repository has received 21 separate undocumented edits.

This is a library of general-purpose containers and allocators that other programs build on. Nothing about how it is called changed and nothing about the callers changed. Containers now hand back values that were never put into them, lose values that were, miscount what they hold, and in places refuse or crash on work they used to complete.

Putting values in goes wrong in several shapes. Appending a value to a chain of elements linked in both directions, through the plain call that takes only the value, puts it at the front rather than after the last, so the order read back is reversed; a chain linked in one direction only misplaces it the same way. Putting a value on the front of a collection open at both ends leaves the reported count untouched, so a container holding elements reports zero and looks empty to anything that checks before it reads, and first-in-first-out use layered over it undercounts the same way. Putting a value into a store of fixed capacity that reuses its slots in rotation also leaves the count at zero while room remains, and it only starts rising once the store is nominally full.

Taking values back out is no better. Reading from that rotating store advances two slots each time, so every other value comes back and the ones in between are lost. Taking the top element, over and over, off a collection meant to give up its eleme
